note.p: Macmillan was one of Godwin's printers. The fourth edition of Godwin's book The Pantheon: or Ancient History of The Gods of Greece and Rome (1814) was printed by B. Macmillan of Bow Street, Covent Garden. However, there are no printers called Macmillan on The British Book Trade Index that match the dates. However, there is B McMillan app 1773 trading until 1834 at various addresses: 35 Henrietta St. Cr Exeter Change, Strand. 11 Tavistock St, Covent Gdn. Russell Ct. 6 Bow St.
One instance of Macmillan occurs in 1800 which precedes the majority of the contacts by five years; thus, it may not be the same person.

See clarification from Ed Pope: Godwin saw the printer frequently between 1805 and 1826 and took tea with him once in 1822, otherwise it was some 250 calls. The printer's full name was Buchanan Macmillan, he was printer of the Sun newspaper in 1805 and imprisoned for a month for printing a libel against Earl St Vincent. His will PCC 1832 printer of Covent Garden. The 1805 to 1812 entries above were probably him but using McMillan instead of Macmillan
